content.text: {"headline":"Approve P1: no-cost rebalancing keeps both queues above the 80% target through 12:45–15:30","why":"Payments lost capacity to a flu-driven sick wave (11 absences vs a usual 2; agents fell from 36 to 24, below the 28–29 planned), and service level dipped to 60.3% at 12:30. Demand is only modestly up (+6%), so this is a capacity gap. The model predicts the disruption window recovers even with no action (85.7%), but P1 adds a margin at zero cost. It moves 2 cross-skilled agents from general to payments 13:00–14:00, delays payments breaks 13:45–14:30 by 45 minutes and runs IVR callback on payments 15:00–16:00. Predicted service level is 87.0% overall (payments 87.9%, general 85.9%), abandon rate falls to 2.8% from 3.6%, and rest of day is 92.7%. No policy issues; no escalation needed.","trade_offs":["P0 (no action) also meets target at 85.7% for ₹0, but abandons are higher (3.6% vs 2.8%) and payments has less buffer if more sickness is logged.","P2, P3 and P4 push payments to 92–95% and cut abandons to 2.0–2.4%, but cost ₹1,815–2,535 in overtime for a target P1 already meets for free.","General is not hurt by lending 2 agents in P1: its predicted service level is 85.9% vs 85.4% with no action.","Delayed breaks put some extra load on payments agents, who are already short-staffed."],"watch":"Watch payments agent count and service level each interval from 13:00. If more absences arrive or payments drops back toward 80%, switch to P4 (₹1,815, payments 92.4%), the cheapest overtime option. Also check general stays above 80% while its 2 agents are on payments."}
